item.text: Those tests don't flake (60 runs clean) — which fits: with a protocol-3 leader the config entry *is* an FSM log, so the preceding `EnsureSame` closes the race. Let me record that.

Turn complete. Report updated at [report.md](/home/nitro/Desktop/consensus-assurance/baseline/runs/2026-10-09_14-01-25-hashicorp_raft-baseline/work/report.md).

This turn I nailed down why the frozen-`peerSet` defect only surfaces in the upgrade test, which sharpens Finding 1 into a coherent, confirmed local defect.

The frozen reference in `EnsureSamePeers` is only stale if a node lags at the instant it is read, and the preceding `c.EnsureSame(t)` normally closes that window because a committed `LogConfiguration` entry is delivered to the FSM and `EnsureSame` waits for every node's FSM to see it. But `prepareLog` in `raft.go` only forwards `LogConfiguration` to the FSM when `r.protocolVersion > 2`. In `TestRaft_ProtocolVersion_Upgrade_2_3` the leader runs with `ProtocolVersion = 2`, so the config entry is not an FSM log, `EnsureSame` returns without waiting for it, and the window stays open for `EnsureSamePeers` to snapshot a stale 2-voter `peerSet`.

That prediction was testable, so I ran it: the tests that share the helper but use protocol-3 leaders — `TestRaft_JoinNode`, `TestRaft_JoinNode_ConfigStore`, `TestRaft_RemoveFollower_SplitCluster` — passed **60/60 combined runs** (`work/.runtime/join_c20.log`). Only the protocol-2 upgrade path flakes. So the defect is a genuine latent bug in the shipped `EnsureSamePeers` helper, with an observable trigger specific to the v2→v3 upgrade path.

Net state of the audit:

- Finding 1 (confirmed, low severity, test-support helper `testing.go:691`): frozen reference peer set makes `EnsureSamePeers` unable to converge if a node lags at the first read; reproduced 6/20 with the real helper and 0/20 with a refresh-each-poll control; goroutine dump shows the cluster was actually consistent. Not a Raft safety/liveness violation.
- No consensus-level defect found: full build/vet clean, all non-network tests pass, and line-by-line review of the commit/vote/pre-vote/replication/snapshot/config/FSM paths matched Raft semantics.
- Residual uncertainty recorded honestly: with the module cache's provenance untrusted, I cannot offline determine whether the frozen-snapshot pattern is the injected mutation or an upstream latent flake.

Next useful work: probe for a consensus-level defect that Finding 1's flake might be masking — e.g. targeted in-memory scenarios around configuration-change commitment and the protocol-2 config path — and confirm no other shipped helper or code path exhibits the same freeze-a-value anti-pattern.
